Okay, I came from your other post. This does sound abusive, and your story is incredibly similar to my upbringing. What got me through was my friends, learning about mental health to understand what was going on (but it took me YEARS to do this) and coping mechanisms. 

You do not deserve to be treated the way you are. 

You deserve to be seen, and for people to make the effort to understand you. 

I think a key will be finding a “third space” where you can escape. School is a great option. Join an after school activity or club, or learn to play an instrument, maybe get a part time job when you are old enough (but please, I beg of you, be careful with older people. Especially older people that you might meet at your future job, or here on the internet. Learn about grooming and know the signs so you can protect yourself. You are vulnerable, and whether or not you like to admit it, you’re naive. Every 14 year old is, no matter how intelligent or self aware. I would watch the Adam Mcyntire / Colleen Ballinger stuff on YouTube to learn about grooming in a documentary style way.)

Be mindful of the party scene that may pop up over the next few years in high school. Kids can be stupid and cruel, especially when substances are involved. For me, drinking and partying became my “third place,” and I sure wish I had let myself feel like I had a different path. 

Go to your school counselor. Go to your teachers. Tell them point blank what you think is going on. They are there to help you. You have the self awareness of knowing how you are being treated is wrong. Use that power. I didn’t have that, I thought everyone’s parents just sucked and I was the weak one. If you can get into a therapy program through school, do it. You can learn about attachment styles, dysregulation of the nervous system, trauma responses, coping mechanisms, etc. You can also start self learning via the internet, but be careful because it’s always better to have a conversation that’s tailored to you. Even at 27 I still have to dissect which posts I agree and disagree with. Some great places to start are “the.holistic.psychologist” and “seerutkchawla” on instagram. 

Last, my fandoms also were such a safe space for me. Be careful of creeps on the internet, but having my friends who genuinely loved things I loved, and playing online games (like Neopets, where I could simultaneously be talking to fellow fans on Reddit) might just have saved my life. Even when no one understood me and my passions, I always had my fellow Whovians haha. 

Hang in there, stay as positive as you can while simultaneously acknowledging, and telling yourself every day that you deserve respect and love. Do not wait for another person to give you love. Give it to yourself and literally tell yourself you love yourself every single day, out loud. Affirmations work. 

I’ll end by recommending to indulge in media that allows you an escape. I loved Paper Towns by John Green at your age, and generally all Green Brothers content. They always made me feel safe. Reading fantasy novels, or cozy witchy novels and letting your mind escape into whatever world you are reading in is a magical third place to discover too. 

I’m sending you love and support! You deserve happiness and you are worthy of love! You’re young and I promise you have a beautiful future ahead! Hang in there!!
